title: Mb17891223f of Martha Ballard's Diary
content: martha ballard's diary view image view frames version dec 23, 1789 december 23, 1789 (wednesday) 23 4 cloudy day. mr ballard went varsalboro evidences cause common wealth joseph north esqr. charg north ye night augst 10 th broke house isaac foster night time ravisht wife foster. trial mrs foster apeard calm, sedate unmovd, standing strong atempts made throw aspercions carrecter. shee oath affirmd north broke open door house perpetrated crime rape ravishment, standing exerting selfe much strength would varsalboro. little snow evng. told shee would expose perhaps ruen self shee told supposed enemy informer informer might miss receivd story relative fack. shee replyd father, mean guilty. would admit admit testemony mrs foster 19 august complaind shee shee [sic] receivd great abuses people unknown throwing stones house, striveing get ye lodg relating abuses worst shee met since mr fosters absence, shee hoped would quite kill could nothing wors unless killd shee also north abused wors person world shee believd best keep troubles selfe mutch shee could till husband returnd shee hopt wd soon. shee also complaind 25 remember day aright) norths treating wors person go woman besids wife, wife jellous relating chargs lais. shee seemd exceedingly troubled shee related tryals, aust question information descend particulars time, last time converst husband absent. 28 inst calld mind mrs foster saying colo north positively unlawfull concourse another woman besides wife begd never mention person, also testified n last weak find diarey ye 18th inst), really believd mrs foster treated shee complains deny charg exhibeted also never least reason suspect virtue modesty jump see excerpts dec. 23 entry chapter 9 practice reading dec. 23 entry 'magic lens' (requires java) see dec. 23 entry martha ballard's diary online

title: Page 285 of The History of Augusta
content: history augusta nash, charles elventon 1904 view image view frames version title page page 285 page 285 mrs. ballard's diary. 285 1789. october 1. company afternoon. mrs. hannah north, mrs. chever, mrs. weston cohors, mr. savage, informs mrs. foster sworn rape number men, among whome shocking, indeed. 2. called 4th h. morn, mrs. goff, travail. walkt davis, store; crost river went land horseback. arived 6th h. old mrs. goff returned boston 1h. p. tarried night. 3. mrs. goff's illness increast, shee safe delivered 11h. 30 m. morn, daughter. marm, mrs. bullen, mrs. ney, asistants. returned home 6, afternoon. find mr. ballard returned tower surveying yesterday. 4. josh sinclair brot us barrel herrin, smokt. 5. informed man drowned jones' eddy came passenger boston capt. howard. 6. thee sweap one mills got crank, neither tended night. 7. mitty devenport dined. joshua sinclare mr. richardson drank tea. 12 years since left oxford. 8. called 8th h. morn, mr. daw's hook, wife travail. regiment troop convened mr. shuball hinkley's land. 9. mrs. daw safe delivered 6th hour morn fine son, weighed 11 lbs. mrs. daw 32d woman putt bed since feb'y 5th. 10. rev'd mr. isaac foster removed vassalboro day. mr. ballard gone hook. mr. densmore's. mr. hatch went 11. day aneversary ordination rev'd isaac foster church flock town three years since. 12. called 12 o'clock, morn, john cuming's. arived 2; found wife safe delivered son, weighed 11 lbs, 5th son 7th child. esquire coney took breakfast informed woman winthrop fell fire burned degree shee soon expired; hallowell girl night 8th inst. fell fire, also, life expected. morning 8th inst. daniel savage's junior oldest son scolt much. 13. called 8th hour, morn, mrs. stone. shee safe delivered 5 p. m. daughter. 2d child; child weighed 3-4 lbs. october 7. submit davenport, twenty years age, daughter jonathan susanna (white) davenport, lived opposite side river ballard family. october 8. title: Page 293 of The History of Augusta
content: history augusta nash, charles elventon 1904 view image view frames version page 293 mrs. ballard's diary. 293 1790. june 17. air. foster sleeps informs esquire hussey departed life yesterday, 7h. p. m. prison. 18. burial esquire hussey. 19. mr. ballard went hook meeting proprietors unity. calvin edson drowned river night; attempted cross nd supposed fell asleep fell board. 20. received letter brother barton 13th inst., informs dear sister debby davis departed life 8th, interred 10th. left husband seven children mourn loss. 21. mr. town mrs. barton went judge boman's office; took administration late husband's estate. mr. edson drowned 21st inst., taken morn. 22. mr. ballard went mr. carr's meeting chuse juriors. mr. carr mager goodin chose grand jury; capt. page andrew goodin petty, etc. 23. brother ebenezer's infant deceased day. july 4. mr. seth williams drank tea 5. capt. stackpool winslow] informs sherebiah town expired last evening, 11 12 hours; interred to-morrow; capt. allso informed mr. lues killed limb falling tree; man penobscott hanged himsef another boston shott 6. left home early, bound pownalboro; mr. ballard, allso. went board leut. pollard's boat; stopt pittstown; got mr. hatch's took lodgings coart's setting. went coart, afternoon. 11. sunday. pownalboro. went mr. hatche's meeting mr. kider's eastern river. 13. came coart house. saw melone receive punishment coart inflicted 8 hour morn; returned mr. hatche's. paid reckoning sett home. wrode mr. pollard's horse. dined mager smith's. called mr. bullin's mr. jackson's. arived home near sun sett. 18. old mr. pitts drank tea june 17. obed hussey lived east side river nearly opposite sheppard's point. april 6, 1789, town meeting approved road river near esquire hussey's house eastward across intervale foot hill, till comes near mr. andrew goodwin's barn, eastward county road." (town records, p. 78.) june 21. calvin edson, came cape cod 1781, last occupied farm afterwards owned allen lambard, present fifth ward. mr. edson first introduce twitch witch grass town; obtained half bushel seed massachusetts, thought valuable vitality, power resist frosts. edson "got something would winter kill." june 26. jonathan bowman, judge probate lincoln county, 1772 death 1804. july 13. flogged whipping post. july 18. seth pitts, senior. (see pitts family.) jump see document 'archive'

title: Page 226 of The History of Augusta
content: history augusta north, james w. 1870 view image view frames version title page page 226 page 226 insert page 227 page 228 page 226 226 general henry sewall 1790. ble langdon new york, died november 10, 1826, leaving family boston. 3. jane caroline, born july 16, 1795, married richard devens charlestown, mass. deceased. 4. mary married charles devens, merchant boston; died october 3, 1849, leaving two sons educated harvard college. eldest, gen. charles devens, graduated harvard 1838, l.l.b. 1840; served country distinction suppression rebellion. arthur lithgow devens, youngest son, graduated harvard 1840. lawyer, residing new hampshire. 5. fances, born devember 1, 1800, married john l. payson, late american consul messina. 6. frederick born 1807, died age fourteen. henry sewall born “old york” state october 24, 1752. sixth generation lineal descent henry sewall common ancestor sewalls new england, emigrated great britain america settled rowley, mass., 1634. henry's father, york, lived upon small farm pursued mechanical occupation “mason.” passed minority laboring farm acquiring father's trade. breaking revolution, age twenty-three years, enlisted soldier company raised falmouth, portland), may, 1775, soon battle lexington, marched cambridge joined col. phinney's regiment massachusetts line. course three four campaigns passed various subordinate grades captain, rank sustained end war. battle hubbardston retreat ticonderoga, one skirmishes previous surrender burgoyne saratoga, event witness. northern troops ordered south, victory, went pennsylvania joined main army gen. washington white marsh, near philadelphia, november following. wintered valley forge 1778, served remainder war new jersey highlands new york. three last years war, captain, aid-de-camp major general william heath massachusetts. jump see document 'archive'

title: Page 227 of The History of Augusta
content: history augusta north, james w. 1870 view image view frames version title page page 226 page 226 insert page 227 page 228 page 227 1790. general henry sewall 227 immediately war, september, 1783, came fort western hallowell opened store connection william burley beverly, east side river near foundry, continued five years business, went new york, 15th august, 1788, opened office number five water street purpose buying selling public securities, accumulated rapidly depreciated hands failed. returned hallowell chosen town clerk, office held town augusta thirty-five years, time several years one selectmen. appointed kinsman, judge david sewall, clerk district court maine organization 1789, held office twenty-nine years, resigned 1919 judge appinted organization kennebec county 1799, chosen register deeds, held office seventeen years, succeeded 1816 john hovey. hel held succession commissions division inspector, brigadier major-general eighth division militia, comprising counties lincoln, kennebec somerset thirty years, resigned military office william king, first governor maine, upon new organization militia. one church formed hallowell--south parish--over rev. mr. gillet ordained august 1795, appointed deacon september following, continued member officer therein--an advocate doctrine free sovereign grace.”1 gen. sewall large frame strong features expressive firmness, decision military bearing, particularly mounted horseback. john o. page hallowell, one aids, presented noble white charger upon general made impoing spirited figure, short bow-legs appear good advantage foot. faithful diligent performance duties offices held. clerical officer seldom excelled. wrote round uniform plain hand gave records appearance great neatness accuracy. upright, conscientious, pious rigidly orthodox 1ms. autobiographical sketch, red book hist. soc. coll. jump see document 'archive'

title: Page 228 of The History of Augusta
content: history augusta north, james w. 1870 view image view frames version title page page 226 page 226 insert page 227 page 228 page 228 1790. general henry sewall 227 religious views. towards close life religious rigor much softened. lafayette, nation's guest, reached portland 1825, gen. sewall, well acquainted army, went see warily approached crowd intending first make known, lafayette saw recognized perceiving design exclaimed, "ah! henry sewall can't cheat embraced, aged soldiers wept. sewall kept diary many years briefly entered notices events business family matters. including dates 1784 1820, came writer's hands used preparing history. gen. sewall married tabitha sewall, cousin, daughter john sewall georgetown, february 9, 1786; died, married rachel crosby salem, mass., another cousin, june 3, 1811. died june 15 1830, aged seventy-seven years, married third wife elizabeth lowell, daughter john lowell bosteon, september 9, 1833. survived died 1862 advanced age. gen. sewall died september 4, 1845, aged ninety-three years. seven children, first wife, two sons, charles william, five daughters. abigail married eben dutch susanna robert gardiner hallowell. others died young unmarried. jump see document 'archive'

title: The Objections of Henry Sewall's seven objections to Rev. Isaac Foster The Objections
content: henry sewall's seven objections rev. isaac foster sewall, henry oct. 4, 1786 image available view frames version objections trascribed north's history augusta pages 205 206. objections objections doctrines held mr. foster, prepared presented capt. sewall, stated follows: article 1. holding gospel dispensation purchased death christ, order god might accept imperfect obedience creatures, instead perfect one law originally required. 2. denying adam created holy. holding capacity generate holiness series obedience. 3. denying total depravity human nature unregenerate state. holding extent, degree. asserting unregenerate persons moral power, ask, seek, strive, gospel sense; improve common grace obtain special grace. 4. denying doctrine absolute, unconditional election. holding election god's foresight faith good works creatures, discriminating ground title eternal life. 6. denying saint's final perseverance founded power faithfulness god. holding persevere virtue choice, asserting persons may apostatize good beginnings, pursued would lead saving grace. 7. holding heathen, destitute light gospel, really duty worship even though hold plurality deities. paul duty persecuting church, account scripture reproved conduct. transcribed north's history augusta pages 205-206, source stated copy hand writing h. sewall, signed benjamin pettingill, one elders church, several others." jump see objections north's history augusta 'archive'

title: January 21 through January 31, 1787 of Henry Sewall's Diary
content: henry sewall's diary sewall, henry 1776 1842 view image view frames version january 21 january 31, 1787 january, 1787. hallowel. sunday 21. met esq. pettingill's. monday 22. tuesday 23. selectmen met dr. cony's transact town business. wedsday 24. sued wm. fletcher, jac. huston, d. emory. &c. thursday 25. mr. prudens wife called friday 26. mr. emerson georgetown called way norridgewalk. saturday 27. complaint revd. foster, mr. t. sewall, summoned appear justice north, answer complaint. day far spent time evidences collected, found necessary adjourn monday morning. sunday 28. met esq. pettingill's. monday 29. trial came charged reporting mr. foster liar could prove facts pretend deny. provided evidence prove assertion thought though mr. north pleased think otherwise. judgement fined fifteen shillings pay costs tria appealed. mr. t. sewall fined 12/ costs. appeal. jump see document 'archive'

content: official story chapter 5 foster dismissed reading hallowell town records early september 1788, find foster's relations town deteriorated point officially writing town's officers, offering sever connections town would pay 200 pounds double amount annual salary. town turned leaving issue uncomfortably unresolved. finally see town records october 30, town decided convene church council november hear, judge, advise matters grievances." foster agreed. official record charges presented foster november church council. hints, however, entries martha wrote attending church council meeting. know hallowell's december town records church council recommended dismissing foster, foster insisted town pay 200 pounds requested make counteroffer, town rejected request. foster officially dismissed meeting vote 84 9: "whereas rev. isaac foseter principles behavior given ground opinion town uneasiness complaint againt him....the town hallowell, legal town meeting assembled, therefore...grant rev. isaac foster dismission pastoral office." take note terms dismissal, unusually severe: church sexton directed forbid isaac foster preaching meeting house also forbid setting foot meeting house. previous suits countersuits next although foster didn't set foot meeting house, stay town, haggling terms dismissal. table contents hallowell town records (transcription john sewall) town hallowell officials view text view frames version 86 (sep 9, 1788 mtg) 87 (sep 9, 1788 mtg) folio 86 (september 9, 1788 meeting) jump see document 'archive'

title: The Official Story - Chapter 6
content: official story chapter 6 foster haggles town following year, foster remained town, haggling terms dismissal. committee appointed town settle issue. (note judge north ephraim ballard committee item #5, p. 173.) seems, however, committee unable resolve foster's settlement. martha keep track town's financial wrangling foster? ten months foster's dismissal, group foster's friends proposed town re-hear case. looking agenda town meeting early october 1789 (item #2), see town refused re-open case. meeting (items #3 4), town appointed another committee handle "demands relative civil contract town mr. foster." committee included henry sewall. others empowered consider foster's request letters ministers boston judge sullivan." letters, unfortunately, haven't survived. business hand clearly pressing. meeting adjourned, present agreed meet six days later. point, town accepted report committee, appointed another committee "carry report execution." present october 12 agreed meet several weeks later, financial terms settlement finally agreed upon. minutes meeting, however, don't tell us terms martha, meticulous accounts keeper, record amount finally paid rev. mr. foster. however, find town meeting voting following april "raise 150 pounds" purpose satisfying obligation given mr. isaac foster, defraying necessary town charges." previous foster dismissed next meanwhile, however, isaac foster's debts mounting... table contents
